title: Data-Only Execution and Analog Circuit Theory Closing Software Development
description:
Software development has an unsolved problem: code grows without bound. Every application requires code. Every code addition expands the interaction surface. Every interaction surface expansion produces new categories of defects. Seventy years of software engineering methodology — structured programming, object-oriented design, functional programming, type systems, formal verification, automated testing — has reduced the growth rate. None has stopped it. This paper identifies why the growth cannot stop within the code paradigm and traces a path that exits the paradigm entirely. The path originates in analog circuit theory, passes through exhaustive domain enumeration of every engineering problem software must solve, produces a sealed compiled infrastructure parameterised entirely through data records, and terminates in a system where all application behaviour is authored as data with zero code. The paper is addressed to researchers who want to understand why this closure is achievable, what properties make it achievable, and what architectural decisions are required to reproduce it.
